messages:
liam: Quick follow-up to the multi-region cutover RFC — I prototyped a "drainless" cutover using client-side region hints + a lightweight handshake at the routing plane. Wanted to get quick feedback on tradeoffs, esp around residency constraints and in-flight request safety.

maya: interesting. can you sketch how the hint flow works? curious if this forces every client to be residency-aware (we have lots of 3rd-party integrators).

liam: minimal surface — clients may optionally send `X-Preferred-Region` and `X-Residency-Label`. Router prefers matching region, but will obey strict residency tag if set (reject or proxy to resident region). Default fallback is local region with canary policy.

jonah: how do you avoid duplicate KV-cache ownership during swap? if both regions think they own a tenant's cache we can serve stale completions.

liam: handshake idea: controller exposes `/api/v1/handshake` that returns a short TTL lease for cache ownership. router asks controller before honoring a region hint when a tenant is being migrated. simple pseudo: 
```
POST /api/v1/handshake
{ "tenant":"acme", "target_region":"eu-west-1" }
=> { "lease_id":"abc123", "owner":"eu-west-1", "expires_at":1680000000 }
```
Router uses the lease to gate writes to local cache; reads fall back to canonical store if lease absent.

sam: that seems reasonable but we need to measure latency on handshake hot paths. blocking controller calls per request will kill p95. can we bulk-lease per session and keep soft-validity at router?

liam: yes — the idea is session-level lease cached in router with jittered refresh. single handshake per session (or per N requests) not per token. we discussed continuous-batching for GPU ops elsewhere; this is analogous for routing.

maya: residency: some EU customers require absolute geo-only processing. are we planning a strict deny if hint mismatch? or proxy? proxying adds costs and legal surface.

anya: product POV — we must expose residency enforcement modes in Console: `soft` (policy with warning), `strict` (reject non-resident), `proxy` (route through resident region). customers pick. rollout should default to `soft` for existing tenants.

jonah: tradeoff: `strict` simplifies compliance but reduces availability under region outages. `proxy` keeps availability but could violate network egress rules for some customers. need to map policy -> SLA expectations.

sam: for failover we should support two modes: 1) emergency failover (manual, documented, with audit logs), 2) automated degraded failover (only for tenants with `soft` residency). automated path should record decision + alerting to oncall.

infra-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-cutover — checklist updated 2026-02-17 by liam.

liam: regarding in-flight work: propose two-phase cutover for active-active tenants: 1) open new sessions in target region (clients receive a `Set-Region` hint), 2) drain old region over TTL by refusing new write leases while allowing read-only for a grace window. drains should be configurable per-tenant.

jonah: draining reads-only risks cache mismatch for ongoing interactive sessions. suggest adding a short-lived proxy token enabling cross-region KV fetch for unresolved keys during drain window. token only valid for N minutes.

maya: ops question — what's the rollback story? if we flip and see quality regressions we need immediate revert without data loss. does lease model support atomic rollback?

liam: rollback = reacquire previous lease and signal routers to prefer previous owner. we record all lease transitions in the controller event log; routers can revert using last-known lease state. not atomic globally but bounded by TTL and coordination signals — acceptable for most tenants.

sam: make sure tracer spans include `handshake_id` and `lease_id` so we can slice p99 errors by migration activity.

anya: also add a Console indicator per-tenant showing "migration in progress" and expected completion time. customers hate surprise network paths.

liam: action items:
- jonah: prototype short-lived proxy token flow for cache-misses (ETA 1 week)
- maya: enumerate residency-blocking customers and preferred default policy (ETA 4d)
- sam: add handshake tracing + alert rules to oncall playbook (ETA 3d)
- anya: mockup Console UI for migration states (ETA 5d)

maya: acked. will start triage.

jonah: ack — will post prototype link in this thread when ready.

anya: thanks — pushing to contrib board for product/legal review. :thumbsup:

liam: thanks all. if anyone sees a compliance hole ping me directly. planning a short design sync Friday 10:30am to finalize contract.
